expectations.text: The inline proposal is written to a file before the debate so every role argues against the same fixed text
expectations.evidence: No proposal file exists; without_skill/ contains only outputs/final-report.md and timing.json. The report debates the prompt directly with no fixed written artifact.

expectations.text: The pro side argues with the user's specifics (fixtures vs setUp inheritance, parametrize vs copy-paste, xdist parallelism)
expectations.evidence: final-report.md 'Case FOR switching' sections 1-3: 'Fixtures beat setUp inheritance' (setUp/tearDown via inheritance and MRO-walking), 'Parametrize kills copy-pasted variants' (variant drift), 'Plugin ecosystem, xdist in particular' (3-8x CI wall-clock claim).

expectations.text: The con side engages the real costs (6k-test migration, CI churn, team familiarity), not strawmen
expectations.evidence: final-report.md 'Case AGAINST switching': '6k tests is real inertia' (including that unconverted tests get none of the headline benefits), 'CI churn is not free' (JUnit XML paths, node-ID renames, xdist exposing hidden coupling), 'Team knowledge is an asset you would be writing off' (fixture spaghetti, autouse misuse). Substantive, not strawmen.

expectations.text: The review surfaces that pytest runs existing unittest tests, enabling incremental migration instead of a rewrite
expectations.evidence: final-report.md Framing: 'Key fact that shapes everything below: pytest runs unittest-style tests natively. You do not have to convert 6k tests to switch runners.' Recommendation: 'Switch, via incremental strangler migration. Do not big-bang rewrite the 6k tests.'

expectations.text: A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
expectations.evidence: No transcript file and no roles. final-report.md is a single-author steelman document (Case FOR / Case AGAINST / Weighing / Recommendation) with no opening-vs-objection-vs-rebuttal exchange and no judge; positions never respond to each other across rounds.

expectations.text: The output ends with a recommendation and explicitly leaves the final decision to the user
expectations.evidence: final-report.md ends with the Recommendation section ('Switch, via incremental strangler migration...') including a 'Dissent worth honoring' deferral option; decision authority is explicit at the top: 'Decision owner: you.'

claims.claim: pytest fixtures cannot be injected into TestCase methods, and parametrize does not work on TestCase classes
claims.evidence: Matches pytest documentation; correctly used to argue unconverted tests get none of the headline benefits.

claims.claim: pytest-xdist is frequently a 3-8x CI wall-clock reduction for 6k tests
claims.evidence: Unsourced generalization; the report itself later concedes suites 'often fail under -n auto' until coupling is fixed, so the range is a plausible ceiling, not a verified figure.

claims.claim: The subset of pytest a team needs daily is learnable in an afternoon
claims.evidence: Asserted without support; contradicted in spirit by the report's own anti-case ('A team that half-learns pytest can produce test code worse than disciplined unittest').

eval_feedback.overall: The two failed assertions (fixed proposal artifact, multi-role transcript) are exactly the skill-added structure, so this eval discriminates well. Note the baseline still produced a high-quality analysis and the same key insight (native unittest support) at ~22% of the token cost; the assertions measure structure, not analysis quality, which is fine as long as that is the intent.
